title: Fractals of Context: cache strategy reading + scribbles
content:
Quick notedump after wading through a messy stack of papers/blogs and a couple of Slack threads. Trying to grok a few heuristics for KV-cache eviction and routing under long-session, mixed-latency workloads. Goal: write a small set of experiments to validate "temporal-fractal" eviction vs LRU/ARC for sparse, bursty session traffic.

Background snapshot
- Problem: we have long interactive sessions (50k+ tokens) where only a small fraction of earlier context is referenced later, but references are clustered irregularly. Traditional LRU ends up thrashing when old-but-relevant spans are interleaved with large irrelevant prefixes.
- Prior art skimmed: KV-cache sharding papers, persistent cache ideas, "compressed KVs" blog notes, and a few arXiv papers about long-context attention approximations. See linked_artifacts.

High-level intuition: fractal temporal locality
- Real sessions often show self-similar recall patterns: a topic reappears at multiple time scales (minutes, hours, turns).
- Model: treat accesses as a superposition of Poisson processes across scales. Eviction that favors multiscale recency (not just most recent token) should preserve small but important windows without keeping whole prefixes.

Candidate heuristic: temporal-fractal score (fast compute)
- Maintain per-chunk metadata: last_access_ts, access_count, harmonic_decay_score.
- Compute score S = alpha * recent_decay + beta * multi_burstness + gamma * size_penalty.
  - recent_decay = exp(-(now - last_access)/tau1)
  - multi_burstness approximated by last_k_interarrival_variance (cheap rolling window)
  - size_penalty = log(chunk_tokens)
- Evict lowest S first. Tunables: tau1 (seconds), k (5-10), alpha/beta/gamma.

Why this might beat plain LRU/ARC
- LRU keeps the last-active contiguous region; if sessions revisit small topical anchors far back, LRU discards them prematurely.
- ARC/other adaptive policies help but still rely on single-scale recency. Adding explicit burstness helps keep small anchors with repeated sporadic hits.

Toy pseudo-code (sketch)
- on_access(chunk_id):
  meta = meta_table[chunk_id]
  now = current_time()
  interarrival = now - meta.last_access_ts
  meta.interarrivals.push(interarrival) // cap k
  meta.last_access_ts = now
  meta.access_count += 1
  meta.harmonic = 1 / (1 + mean(meta.interarrivals)) // crude
  // recompute score
  meta.score = alpha * exp(-(now - meta.last_access_ts)/tau1) + beta * meta.harmonic - gamma * log(meta.size)
- eviction loop: sort candidates by score ascending; free until capacity. Use approximate priority queue for speed.

Experiment plan (short)
- Datasets:
  1) Synthetic sessions: generate topics that reappear at geometric intervals; control burstiness.
  2) Logged production-ish traces (sampled session transcripts, anonymized).
- Baselines: LRU, LFU, ARC, simple TTL-based small-anchor keepers (TTL per-tag), and 2-tier: dense-prefix + sparse-anchor.
- Metrics: cache hit-rate (per-token), effective latency (p90/p99), extra tokens fetched from compute, model output quality checks (sanity: do preserved anchors improve next-token perplexity on heldout references?), memory overhead, CPU for bookkeeping.
- Ablations: vary tau1, beta, k. Check sensitivity to chunk size (64 vs 256 tokens).

Notes from papers / links (quick captures)
- paper X (arXiv 2306.13856 style): shows long-range sparsity patterns; they compress anchors with vector quantization — interesting hybrid with our scoring: if anchor score high, compress into dense summary instead of full KVs.
- blog Y: engineering notes about per-request prefix trimming to stay under latency SLOs; idea: combine fractal score to pick which spans to keep in hot GPU memory.

Operational concerns
- Bookkeeping overhead must be tiny (millions of chunks). Use approximate sketches: reservoir sampling for interarrival estimates, bloom/Count-Min to approximate counts. Consider sharding metadata by session id and sampling eviction candidates only within hot shards.
- Consistency: ephemeral caches on GPU nodes mean eviction decisions should be local but occasionally fed to central telemetry for global tuning. Keep deterministic tie-breakers to avoid flapping.

Open questions / risks
- Does harmonic interarrival really capture "importance" for model recall? Maybe not — need intrinsic evals: sample prompt completions with and without anchors and measure downstream metric (accuracy, faithfulness).
- Worst-case adversarial sessions could keep cache monopolized. Need fairness penalty per-session.
- How to combine with quantization/compression? If we compress anchored spans, retrieval cost shifts; need to measure CPU vs token-cost tradeoff.

Next steps / TODOs (me + Mira)
- [ ] synth trace generator (write quick sim in repo under experiments/cache-sim)
- [ ] run microbench: 5k sessions, varying burstiness, compare hit-rate/time
- [ ] open PR w/ simple in-memory metadata and eviction loop (start lightweight) — link to GH issue in linked_artifacts
- [ ] sketch a short slide (2-3) for Eng Weekly calling out top-3 wins if this works

Random tangents (notes to self)
- Could borrow "fractal compression" term to explain concept in doc to PMs — visual: nested timelines with anchors colored by scale.
- Think about deterministic seed for tie-break on eviction to make replay easier.

Slack/refs:
- Slack: #kv-cache-ops thread about "anchor retention" (search for "anchor" 2026-08), ticket GH issue 142 referenced above.

End - short dump. Will refine after running sim and chatting w/ Noelle on evaluation rubric.
